title: When I read the Bible, it feels like I am there witnessing the moment…
paragraphs: When I read the Bible, it feels like I am there witnessing the moment…
I stay behind the rocks, barely breathing. The fire flickers low. The desert wind moves gently across the sand. And above us — a sky too vast to measure.
“Look up. Count them… if you can.”

I watch Abraham lift his eyes. I can’t see his thoughts, but I can feel the weight of the promise. Years of waiting. Questions without answers. A body that says “impossible.” A God who says “abundance.”
The stars don’t rush. They don’t strive. They simply burn — steady, countless, faithful.
I remain hidden. Just a witness. Not shaping history. Not part of the covenant. Just observing what faith looks like in its earliest form — trembling but trusting.

How many promises in my life feel just as unreachable?
How often do I measure possibility by my limits instead of His?
The same sky that covered Abraham covers me now…
What if the impossible is simply where faith learns to breathe?
